text:
anna: incident-bot: SEV=critical - continuous-batcher memory surge in us-west-2. p95 latency 2.8s -> 14s, queue depth spiking, some pods restarted by OOM killer. paging and customer errors reported.

incident-bot: [ALERT] continuous-batcher.accumulator_tokens > 2M for 8m on pool 'usw2-batch'. Affected nodes: batch-21,batch-22,batch-23. Auto-recover attempts: 2.

raj: seeing repeated CUDA `cuMemAlloc` failure on batch-22: `cuMemAlloc failed: out of memory (2)`. Container `batcher-runtime` exit 137 at 08:42:11 PDT. Logs: https://logs.redwood/incoming/4160009999-batcher

david: customers `stripe-payments` and `mosaic-ai` reported 503s and degraded throughput. Opening ticket INC-6591. Quick customer-impact: ~900 failed requests across two tenants between 08:40-08:48.

anna: take node ops: cordon+drain batch-22, don't delete emptydir yet. We'll want to collect core and heap before full eviction. `kubectl cordon batch-22 && kubectl drain batch-22 --ignore-daemonsets --grace-period=60`

ops-bot: suggested runbook step: if accumulator growth, enable conservative backpressure and reduce accumulation window. See runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/continuous-batcher#memory-surge

raj: trying backpressure toggle via admin endpoint: `curl -X POST https://internal-api/redwood/v1/admin/backpressure -d '{"enable":true, "drain_rate":0.5}'` -> 202 accepted. Observed inflight drop from ~420 -> ~210 in 45s.

anna: good. Can we avoid full restart? collect heap with `gcore` on the PID before it dies. raj, can you ssh to batch-21 and run `gcore -o /tmp/batcher-core $(pidof batcher-runtime)` if process still alive.

raj: ran gcore on batch-21; uploaded core to S3: s3://rdw-cores/4160009999/batch-21-core.gz. Also grabbed `ps` snapshot: resident memory 32G on batch-21 (expected 10G).

david: initial analysis: accumulator appears to retain references for ACKed requests when stream-chunking interacts with large-sequence clients. Repro on staging with synthetic long-stream workload.

anna: mitigation steps: 1) backpressure enabled (done) 2) toggle `kv_cache.size=small` to reduce GPU-side allocations 3) temporarily route high-token-volume customers to fallback-smaller-model via routing rules.

raj: toggled KV cache: `kubectl patch cm batcher-config -n redwood --patch '{"data":{"kv_cache_mode":"reduced"}}'` then `kubectl rollout restart deployment/batch-runtime -n redwood --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"rollout-ts":"4160009999"}}}}}'` -> rollout in progress.

ops-bot: note: rolling restart may cause transient increase in inflight due to rebalancing. Keep throttle on.

david: added a temporary validator to drop requests with >8000 tokens; canary deployed to 3 instances. This prevented one particularly large customer stream from entering accumulation.

anna: timeline update for customers: posting to #customer-impact draft - "We experienced elevated latency and errors in us-west-2 due to resource exhaustion on our continuous-batcher service from ~08:40-08:50 PDT. Mitigations are active; we routed affected traffic to a fallback model and are collecting a full RCA." ping @support-team for outbound comms. 

incident-bot: [Handoff] current on-call anna -> next on-call oliver at 09:00 PDT.

anna: Oliver, handing off with current state: backpressure=true, kv_cache=reduced, validator applied, batch-22 cordoned (core captured), rollout started to reduce KV allocations. Monitoring dashboard: https://dash.redwood/teams/eng-oncall/incidents/4160009999. Key alerts to watch: accumulator_tokens, cuda_errors, pod_restart_count.

oliver: acknowledged. I'll watch for 30m and escalate to runtime team if pods continue OOMing. What's rollback plan for the config changes?

raj: rollback: 1) backpressure=false API call, 2) patch cm to previous kv_cache_mode, 3) remove token-length validator. But prefer to keep throttles for 30-60m to ensure steady downtrend.

david: pushed hotfix branch that fixes `ack_pending` clear path in accumulator and adds guardrails for streaming chunk references. CI green, canary on 3 pods looks stable (no memory creep in 10m). Git: https://git.redwood/repo/accumulator/commit/7e9c2f.

raj: plan to roll hotfix to 25% -> 50% -> 100% if metrics look good. I'll coordinate gradual rollout and post progress here.

ops-bot: reminder: if rollout causes unexpected CPU/latency regressions, trigger auto-rollback by setting `rollout.maxUnavailable=0`.

anna: thanks team. I'm closing the incident chat and moving to postmortem channel once the hotfix is fully rolled. Will file RCA and link cores/logs.

oliver: monitoring looks stable at 09:15 PDT, p95 down to 300ms, accumulator_tokens trending to normal. I'll keep watch for 1h then mark incident as resolved if steady.

incident-bot: [RESOLVED?] alert cleared for continuous-batcher.accumulator_tokens on pool 'usw2-batch' at 09:22 PDT.

anna: final notes for RCA: root cause = accumulation path retaining references on streaming ACKs for very long sequences; contributing factors = missing request-length validation, default kv_cache sizing for newer model, and no automatic per-customer token cap. Actions: hotfix to accumulator (deployed), add request validator (deployed), add customer routing fallback (done), runbook improved to include `gcore` capture steps, postmortem in 48h.

pager: INC-6591 updated with mitigations, cores, and link to postmortem.

anna: handing off to oliver for the watch window. Thanks all. :heart:
